uncertainties: THE EntA STEP IS ABSENT FROM THIS PAPER'S ROUTE, AND I DID NOT ADD IT. The paper announces 'Here are the 4 steps of enterobactin biosynthesis' and its four steps are EntC, EntB, EntE and the EntD/EntE/EntF assembly. There is no dehydrogenation step and no EntA reaction. Confirmed by substring census over the whole 68,085-character file: 'dehydrogenase' occurs 0 times, 'NAD' occurs 0 times, and the capitalised token 'EntA' occurs exactly ONCE, inside a reference title (Pakarian & Pawelek 2016). Lowercase 'entA' occurs three times: in the operon gene list, in the string 'entA-entF' in the Fur section, and as a Pectobacterium atrosepticum deletion mutant. Emitting an EntA reaction from this paper would be completing the canonical pathway from memory.

The paper does assert that entA 'encodes an enzyme essential for the production of enterobactin' as part of the six-gene operon list. That is the ONLY thing it says about EntA. I deliberately did not turn this into a detailed_in_paper:false subprocess, because the paper's own four-step scheme explicitly omits the stage and inventing a slot for it would license exactly the fabrication above. A reviewer who wants the gap represented should represent it as a GAP, not as a stage.

THE PAPER USES 'DHB' FOR TWO DIFFERENT MOLECULES. The numbered body step says EntB 'converts isochorismate into 2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate (DHB)'. The Figure 1 caption says the pathway includes 'formation of 2,3-dihydroxybenzoate (DHB) by EntB'. Those are different compounds. The route is therefore chemically BROKEN as written: nothing in this paper converts 2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoate onward, and R3 chains to R2 only through the abbreviation collision. I recorded both molecules and did not resolve the contradiction.

L-SERINE IS NEVER MENTIONED. 'serine' occurs 0 times in the entire file, in any case. The paper nonetheless says three DHB molecules are assembled 'into the cyclic trilactone structure of enterobactin'. The source of the trilactone core is therefore unstated. I did not add serine to R5.

ATP IS NEVER NAMED AS A REACTANT. The token 'ATP' occurs exactly once in the file, inside a reference title about ATP synthase. R3 is an adenylation with no adenyl donor stated, so ATP is NOT listed as an important participant here, even though it is in PMC12096016 where the paper does name it.

PYRUVATE IS NEVER MENTIONED (0 occurrences), so R2 has one product where the chemistry has two. Likewise 'hydrolysis', 'water' (as a reactant) and 'Mg'/'magnesium' are absent, so R2 has no water and R1 has no metal cofactor. THIS PAPER NAMES NO COFACTOR OF ANY KIND for any biosynthetic step; the secondary_participants list contains regulators and iron species only, and that emptiness is itself the finding.
EntB is called 'isochorismatase' in the biosynthesis section and 'isochorismate lyase' in the antibiotic section. These are one protein, not two.

This paper says EntB 'functions as a carrier protein, binding DHB for subsequent steps'. It asserts BINDING only. It never asserts covalent attachment of the aryl group to a carrier domain and never asserts a transfer of the loaded group from EntB to EntF. I therefore created no loading or transfer reaction here, even though PMC12096016 supports both.

R4 (EntD priming) is a PROTEIN modification, not a metabolite conversion, and the paper gives neither the modified residue nor the phosphopantetheine donor. A consumer expecting only small-molecule conversions should expect to filter it.
S5 (regulation) is regulation, not chemistry, and carries no reaction ids; low confidence, consistent with how I treated the regulatory findings in the other papers of this set.

CROSS-PAPER DISCIPLINE, STATED EXPLICITLY: PMC12096016 is the other enterobactin paper in my set and it DOES supply the EntA reaction, pyruvate as the EntB co-product, ATP for the EntE adenylation, L-serine for the EntF condensation, Mg2+ for EntC, the covalent ArCP loading and the EntB-to-EntF transfer. NONE of that was carried into this file. Every entry above rests on a quote from THIS paper's own full_text, and the omissions above are recorded as omissions.
